rerun_reason: Confirming rerun for the level changes the first pass authored but could not verify (that machine could not rebuild the ROM). Since the first pass: TYRANTRUM offset 1->2, OMASTAR 2->3, and AERODACTYL 0->2 - the follow-up the first pass recommended and the main agent approved. The headless ROM also now carries the AI setup/support pricing and the healthy-turn-one-switch charge.

party_changed_from_first_pass.reason: Chronology, not difficulty. The first-pass party used MAGEARNA (legendary_sign:RustboroCity_DevonCorp_2F - the Devon stairs are blocked until FLAG_RETURNED_DEVON_GOODS, which is set after Rusturf Tunnel, i.e. after this battle) and WHIMSICOTT (Cottonee's only source is wild:VerdanturfMeadow, C20 at cap 30). Neither is holdable by a player standing in Rustboro Gym. Removing them is what made this fight honest: Magearna was the body that resisted or was immune to Rock, Flying, Dragon, Normal and Fairy simultaneously and single-handedly swept the first pass.

attempts.narrative: Mega Aerodactyl still died on turn 1 (Bullet Punch plus Psychic), but Carbink's Body Press took Lucario with it. Relicanth then decided the fight on its own: Choice Band, Rock Head, 252 Speed and a 150 BP Head Smash, which outsped and one-shot Ludicolo (59 HP, neutral), then Shaymin, then Reuniclus on three consecutive turns. Mr. Mime was down to 4 HP from the Mega's Dual Wingbeat and Cloyster was the last body standing when Omastar and Carbink finished it. Six to two.

attempts.rebuild_reason: Relicanth, not the Mega, is the member that decides the fight, and the r1 party carried no Intimidate and nothing that resisted Rock. Arcanine (Growlithe from Route 103 plus the Rustboro Fire Stone) was added for Intimidate and 95 base Speed, and Cloyster was moved to the lead so a 4x Icicle Spear answers the Mega without spending the Psychic lane.
attempts.narrative: Intimidate on entry changed the first turn completely - see the strategy checks. Cloyster put the Mega to 5 HP and Extreme Speed finished it on turn 2. Carbink's Body Press under its own Reflect was the real grinder, killing Cloyster and half of Ludicolo and Arcanine; Omastar under Tailwind outsped and removed Ludicolo. Shaymin's Earth Power cleared Carbink and a 4x Seed Flare cleared Relicanth before it ever chose a second move. Bombirdier's Knock Off removed Reuniclus. Arcanine came back in for a second Intimidate and a spread Dazzling Gleam finished Tyrantrum and Bombirdier together. Four player faints out of six against a full six-member sweep.

protect_note: Roxanne's side used Protect zero times across both runs, as in the first pass. Aerodactyl and Omastar both carry it; Aerodactyl spent its turns on Tailwind and Rock Slide and Omastar on Muddy Water and Ice Beam, in every case because an attack or the speed move scored better than guarding. There is no empty guarding to report on this trainer.
ai_observations: The AI played this trainer well in both runs and there is no decision I would call a defect. The Intimidate-conditional Tailwind on r2 turn 1 is the best single AI choice I saw anywhere in this block: the same battler, on the same turn of the same fight, attacked when its Attack was untouched and set Tailwind when its Attack had been dropped.

Standing question for the AI owner, carried over and now sharpened: Tyrantrum has still never fired Earthquake beside an airborne partner across two passes, although r2 turn 7 presented exactly that board. Either the authored pairing needs Earthquake to score higher than a same-target Head Smash, or the plan line should stop describing it as a signature of this team.

ai_decision_frames_max was 61-62 (about 1.03 s) in both runs. The first pass on this trainer measured 8 frames. That is roughly an 8x increase on the same boards. Correctness looks better; the cost is a visible pause. Reported as a sampled measurement, not a worst case.

level_changes.rule_applied: Lost one optimized attempt, then won the second with four player faints out of six. That is emphatically the brief's 'won after a real fight' band, and it is the first loss recorded anywhere in this block. Keep the current offsets.
level_changes.verdict: The three level changes carried into this rerun (Tyrantrum 1->2, Omastar 2->3, Aerodactyl 0->2) are CONFIRMED CORRECT and should stand. The Mega now enters at the player's cap instead of two levels under it, survives long enough to choose between attacking and setting Tailwind, and the fight no longer resolves as a one-body sweep. No further change; the per-member +/-2 budget for this pass is now spent on Aerodactyl (+2) and half spent on Tyrantrum and Omastar (+1 each).
level_changes.honest_caveat: Part of the difficulty swing between passes comes from the party, not the levels: removing the chronology-illegal Magearna removed the body that resisted five of this team's six attacking types. The levels and the legal-party correction are both real, and I cannot separate their contributions from two runs. What is certain is that at these levels, against a party a player could actually field in Rustboro, this leader is a genuine fight rather than a sweep.

cooler_note: The first pass called out type monotony and recommended putting Ground pressure on the field early. This rerun says something more specific: the team's problem was never the concept, it was that one illegal Steel body hid how good the team already is. Against a legal party, Carbink's Body Press under its own Reflect and Relicanth's Choice Band Head Smash are two genuinely distinct pressure engines, and the Tailwind branch gives the Mega a real second life. The one weak note remains Tyrantrum: it is the team's Earthquake carrier and its airborne partners exist to make that safe, but it has now twice chosen a single-target Head Smash instead. If the Earthquake line is meant to be the team's signature, that pairing wants to be set up earlier - leading Tyrantrum beside Bombirdier rather than deploying both last would give the tactic a board to happen on. Species-wise the six are well chosen and worth preserving.
